title: Payments Reconciliation Engine
arch: Scheduled DAG · idempotent matching across multiple provider feeds · exception queue for human review
role: Designed the matching model and owned the rollout
impact: 1.4M transactions/cycle · 3 days of manual work → 20 minutes
desc: Automated a month-end reconciliation process that previously occupied two analysts for three days.

slides.title: Project Overview
slides.lead: Automated a month-end reconciliation that previously occupied two analysts for three full days.
points: Matching across multiple provider feeds with differing schemas
Exception queue for the genuinely ambiguous cases
Designed the matching model and owned the rollout
Ran in parallel with the manual process for two cycles before cutover

slides.title: Architecture
slides.lead: A scheduled DAG, deliberately idempotent so any cycle can be re-run safely.
notes: Each stage writes to its own table; nothing mutates in place
Matching is deterministic — same inputs always produce the same result
Airflow retries are safe because every task is idempotent

slides.title: Key Results
slides.lead: The work moved from three days of spreadsheet comparison to a twenty-minute run.
points: Analysts now review exceptions rather than hunting for them
Month-end close moved forward by two business days

title: Event Router
arch: Event-driven · 3 services · at-least-once delivery with replay from offset
role: Sole backend engineer on the service
desc: Fans internal state changes out to downstream consumers with replay when a consumer falls behind.

slides.title: Project Overview
slides.lead: A routing layer that fans internal state changes out to downstream consumers, with replay when a consumer falls behind.
points: Replaced a nightly batch export that left consumers up to 24h stale
Three services: ingest, router, replay coordinator
At-least-once delivery with idempotency keys on the consumer side
Sole backend engineer across design, build and operation

slides.title: Architecture
slides.lead: Producers publish once; the router owns fan-out, ordering guarantees and replay.
notes: Partitioned by entity id so per-entity ordering is preserved
Replay reads from a stored offset rather than re-publishing
Kubernetes HPA on consumer lag, not CPU

slides.title: Key Results
slides.lead: Steady-state throughput held while the failure modes got far less dramatic.
points: Replay turned a 3-hour incident recovery into a 5-minute operation
Consumer teams onboarded themselves using the published contract
